To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scaffold design of trivalent chelator head dictates affinity and stability for labeling His-tagged proteins in vitro and in cells.
the scaffold design of multivalent chelators dictates affinity and kinetic stability, which in turn are crucial for labeling His-tagged proteins at low picomolar concentrations in vitro and in cells.

(1) the design of a scaffold dictates the affinity and stability of the MCH; (2) the scaffold of an MCH determines the optimal probe concentration to label His-tagged proteins in cells; and (3) the scaffold design of an MCH can be used to tune the kinetics of the interaction with His-tags in cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the systematic optimization of the scaffold, linker, chelator head of small chemical/biological interaction pair to achieve the highest possible affinity and kinetic stability.
the design of a new class of multivalent chelators and the optimization of the scaffold design for the highest possible affinity and stability in in vitro as well as cellular systems.
the design of the most stable and selective chemical/biological interaction pair that is compatible with cellular applications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scaffold design of MCHs dictates their affinity and stability for labeling of His-tagged proteins in vitro and in cells.
the scaffold design of MCHs determines their affinity for His-tagged proteins in vitro as well as their stability for labeling His-tagged proteins and proteins of interest in cells.
a scaffold design that allows for the highest flexibility in binding to His tags is the best option to achieve the highest stability in binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a scaffold with a high degree of symmetry is essential for the design of a high-affinity and stable MCH.
the scaffold design of multivalent chelators is crucial for their performance, and the cyclic scaffold provides the best combination of affinity and stability.
the scaffold design of multivalent chelators has a major effect on the affinity and stability of the resulting interaction pairs.
